NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is to modify the anode gas inlet configuration to incorporate a passive water recovery system that captures water from the anode exhaust and recirculates it to the anode inlet, preventing membrane dehydration under high current density. Standard practice uses only cathode humidification with a 10% parasitic load to manage hydration, with no anode-side water management. This is a departure because it leverages the anode exhaust as a water source rather than relying solely on external humidification. The closest existing practice is anode gas recirculation systems in some PEMFCs, but those typically do not incorporate water recovery; this intervention adds a passive water recovery component to the recirculation loop, creating a novel mechanism for internal water balance.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the water balance across the membrane: J_water = J_osmotic - J_electro-osmotic - J_diffusion, where J_water is the net water flux. By recovering water from the anode exhaust (which contains unreacted hydrogen and product water) and returning it to the anode inlet, the intervention increases the anode-side water partial pressure, reducing the net water flux out of the membrane. This maintains membrane hydration at 1.5 A/cm² without increasing cathode humidification. The magnitude verification: at 1.5 A/cm², the electro-osmotic drag coefficient is ~1.1 molecules/electron, and standard anode recirculation without recovery loses ~20% of inlet water. With recovery, this loss is reduced to <5%, sufficient to maintain membrane hydration at 80°C.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- Installation: Replace standard anode recirculation pump with a commercial water-separating recirculation pump (b) mounted at the anode exhaust outlet. Connect the water outlet to a passive capillary wick (b) leading to the anode inlet. Install a mechanical timer (b) to control the recirculation pump duty cycle (c).
- Commissioning: Set the mechanical timer to activate the recirculation pump during high current density operation (>1.2 A/cm²) and deactivate during low load (<0.8 A/cm²) (c). Calibrate the capillary wick flow rate to match the water recovery rate of 0.05 ml/min per A/cm² (c).
- Operation: The system operates passively during high load; no operator intervention required beyond timer setting (c). Maintenance: Inspect capillary wick monthly for clogging (c); replace if flow rate drops >10% (c).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installation: Standard practice requires cathode humidifier installation (1 hour). This intervention adds water-separating recirculation pump installation (1 hour) and capillary wick installation (0.5 hours) – total 1.5 hours (slightly higher but within same burden class due to similar complexity).
- Commissioning: Standard practice requires humidifier calibration (0.5 hours). This intervention adds timer calibration (0.1 hours) and wick flow rate calibration (0.2 hours) – total 0.3 hours (lower burden).
- Operation: Standard practice requires continuous cathode humidifier operation (10% parasitic load). This intervention eliminates cathode humidifier load during anode recovery operation (0% additional parasitic load) – lower burden.
- Maintenance: Standard practice requires humidifier filter replacement (monthly, 0.5 hours). This intervention adds wick inspection (monthly, 0.2 hours) – comparable burden class.
Overall burden: Same installation burden class, lower operation burden, comparable maintenance burden – satisfies same-or-lower burden class constraint.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Operate fuel cell stack at 1.5 A/cm² and 80°C stack temperature for 100 hours with the intervention active, then deactivate for 100 hours as control. Measure membrane ionic resistance hourly via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (existing stack instrumentation). Instruments: Stack temperature sensor (existing), current density meter (existing), impedance analyzer (existing). Pass/fail threshold: Intervention must reduce average ionic resistance by >15% compared to control phase. Kill criterion: If any measurement shows >20% increase in ionic resistance during intervention phase, test fails. Duration: 200 hours total (100 with intervention, 100 without).
